itemListElement.name: Jamie AI Note Taker Review 2026: Bot-Free Meeting Notes Tested for US Teams

mainEntity.name: Is the Jamie AI note taker free?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes: 10 AI notes a month, 30 minutes each. Two things the free plan keeps that rivals charge for: unlimited storage and exports to Google Docs, Notion and OneNote. It also allows 1 custom template and 50 custom vocabulary terms, so names and jargon can be taught early.

mainEntity.name: How much does Jamie AI cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: Billed annually, Jamie Plus costs $24, Pro $46 and Team $37 per seat, each per month, and Enterprise is quoted. The toggle on its pricing page puts the annual saving at 17%, so monthly billing costs more. Pro is the first plan with unlimited notes and 5-hour meetings.

mainEntity.name: Does Jamie join meetings as a bot?

acceptedAnswer.text: No, it records your device audio, so nothing appears in Zoom, Google Meet or Teams. Jamie covers the disclosure gap with a consent email on every plan, while a customized consent notification is Enterprise-only. You still have to start capture, so missed starts mean missed notes.

Yes. Jamie's docs list the mobile app on Google Play alongside the App Store, and recordings sync to desktop instantly. Its pricing page footer, though, offers only Mac, Windows and iPhone downloads, so install Android from Play. Mobile records in-person meetings and runs Ask AI.

Jamie lists notes and transcripts in 99+ languages on every plan, speaker recognition included. Custom vocabulary is where plans diverge: 50 terms on Free, Plus and Pro, 100 on Team and 250 on Enterprise, which matters for names, drug names or product codes in any language.

mainEntity.name: What is a good alternative to Jamie?

acceptedAnswer.text: Granola costs $14 a month for bot-free notes, Fathom records unlimited calls free, and Lynkk pairs bot and bot-free capture with Jira actions for $15 a month. Jamie keeps 2 advantages over all of them: EU-only hosting and 99+ languages.
